app_documentation:
UniStudy is a comprehensive university student study platform designed to facilitate collaborative learning and knowledge sharing among students. The platform serves as a centralized hub where students can upload and share study notes, discover and download educational materials created by their peers, form subject-specific study groups, and engage in real-time discussions with fellow learners. Built with modern web technologies including React for the frontend and Node.js with Express for the backend, UniStudy provides a mobile-responsive experience optimized for both desktop and mobile devices.

The platform's main features include secure user registration and authentication using university email addresses and JWT tokens, a robust notes sharing system with AWS S3 integration for file storage, study group formation and management capabilities, real-time group discussion forums for collaborative learning, and a comprehensive rating and review system to help students identify high-quality study materials. Students can search and filter notes by subject, sort by popularity or rating, bookmark favorite content, and track their contributions through personalized dashboards showing upload statistics and group memberships.

UniStudy is intended for university students seeking to enhance their learning experience through peer collaboration and resource sharing. The platform supports three primary user roles: Students who can upload notes, join groups, and participate in discussions; Group Admins who have additional permissions to manage group members and moderate discussions; and Platform Administrators who oversee the entire system. The application emphasizes ease of use with an intuitive card-based interface, clear visual hierarchy using a purple primary color scheme, and accessibility features meeting WCAG 2.1 AA standards.

The technical architecture leverages PostgreSQL for reliable data storage with a well-structured schema including tables for users, notes, study groups, group memberships, messages, and ratings. All file uploads are securely stored in AWS S3 with database references, ensuring scalability and performance. The platform implements comprehensive security measures including password hashing, email verification, and JWT-based authentication to protect user data and ensure only verified university students can access the system.

glossary.Study Notes: Digital educational materials uploaded by students to the platform, including documents, PDFs, and other file formats stored in AWS S3. Each note includes metadata such as title, subject category, description, author information, upload timestamp, and download count. Notes can be searched, filtered, rated, and downloaded by other students.
glossary.Study Group: A collaborative learning space created by students focused on a specific subject or topic. Groups have a name, subject focus, description, creator (who becomes the initial admin), member list with role assignments, and an associated discussion forum. Groups may have maximum member limits and support both admin and regular member roles.
glossary.Group Admin: A user role within a study group that grants additional permissions beyond regular membership. Group admins can manage group members, approve join requests, moderate discussions, and configure group settings. The group creator automatically becomes the first admin, and additional admins can be designated as needed.
glossary.Note Rating: A quality assessment system allowing students to rate shared notes on a 1-5 star scale and optionally provide written reviews. Each user can rate a note only once, and the system calculates and displays average ratings to help students identify high-quality study materials. Ratings include timestamp tracking and are linked to both the note and the reviewing user.
glossary.JWT Authentication: JSON Web Token-based authentication mechanism used to securely verify user identity and maintain session state. After successful login with valid credentials, the server issues a JWT token that the client includes in subsequent API requests. This stateless authentication approach ensures secure access to protected resources without server-side session storage.
glossary.AWS S3: Amazon Web Services Simple Storage Service used for scalable and secure file storage of uploaded study notes. The platform stores actual file content in S3 buckets while maintaining file URLs and metadata in the PostgreSQL database. This architecture separates file storage from database operations, enabling efficient handling of large files and improved system performance.
